Hi Sanjay — thanks for the note. Below is a concise proposal you can share with your auditors; I've looped in Priyom (persistence) and Kimberly (legal) to confirm the details and provide evidence.

Proposal (operational schedule):
- Hot retention: primary DB and write-ahead logs retained for 30 days for quick restores.
- Warm tier: daily snapshots kept for 90 days (restore window: full restore available within 48h).
- Cold/archival backups: immutable object store for 365 days; these are immutable snapshots used for disaster recovery and regulatory hold.
- Post-365: backups enter a tombstone state and are eligible for purge after 30 days (final purge at ~395 days) unless a legal hold or customer-requested extension is in effect.

Deletion workflow summary:
- Deletion is a two-step workflow: logical deletion (tombstone) -> background secure purge job (overwrite/crypto-erase) -> object-store lifecycle completion. We can provide a short attestation describing the lifecycle and timestamps.

Log-retention exception options:
- We can approve a time-limited exception for incident response with the following guardrails: scoped to specific customer tokens/IDs, audit logging of who requested the extension, and an explicit expiration date (we don't issue indefinite exceptions). For your 180-day ask, that is operationally possible but requires an approval path and acceptance of a documented SOP.

Subprocessors that touch backups/logs (high level):
- CloudZone (object storage) — stores encrypted snapshots;
- TraceStream (log aggregation) — processes telemetry and application logs.
Full CSV attached with versions and dataflow mapping.

I've attached a short PDF proposal and the subprocessor dataflow CSV for your security team. Kimberly, please advise on the DPA language we should hand over to Acme so this aligns with the proposal. Priyom, can you confirm the restore SLAs and the exact purge timeline we operate in practice?

Next steps: if this looks good to you, we'll:
1) Share the short evidence package (S3 bucket audit log, KMS attestations, subprocessor list).
2) Add a limited log-retention exception SOP and route for approval.
3) Provide final language for your DPA addendum.

Best,
Jasmine Liu

Jasmine / Kimberly — technical confirmation below (copied into the thread for Acme):

- Encryption & keys: backups are encrypted at rest with customer-specific DEKs that are wrapped by Redwood KMS keys. For Private deployments we can also support customer-managed keys (BYOK).
- Restore SLA: warm restores (90 day snapshots) typically complete within 24–48 hours depending on snapshot size; cold restores from immutable archives are best-effort and depend on retrieval from Glacier-like tiers (48–120 hours).
- Deletion timeline detail: once a tombstone is created, the object remains marked for 30 days to allow for restores/legal holds; the automated purge job then performs a crypto-erase and removes references from indexes. We retain object-store change logs for 365+30 days to demonstrate the purge progression (matrix attached).
- Subprocessor specifics: CloudZone stores the snapshots in an encrypted bucket (we have a BAA/SaaS DPA with them). TraceStream receives app logs via an encrypted forwarder; persisted logs are subject to the same lifecycle policies. Both vendors support on-demand evidence exports (audit logs, KMS key IDs).

If Acme needs an expanded retention exception (e.g., 180-day log retention for one investigation), our recommended pattern is:
1) Customer submits a signed request to legal/security.
2) Redwood opens a scoped exception ticket that: lists tokens/IDs, start/end date, approver names.
3) Exception is enforced via a temporary policy override and recorded in audit logs.

I've attached the Audit Log Retention Matrix for their review.

— Priyom
Engineering Manager, Persistence

Thanks — a few legal notes for the customer-facing memo:

- DPA alignment: reference Sections 4.2 (data retention) and 6.1 (audit rights) in our standard DPA; propose an addendum paragraph that lists the operational schedule above and the exception workflow. Acme should receive a one-page retention schedule we can attach to the DPA.
- Exception path: approve a scoped, time-bound exception process — we should require: (i) customer-signed exception form; (ii) internal approval from Security + Legal; (iii) an audit trail export at exception close.
- Archive-only holds: for legal/ransom investigations we can mark a backup as 'archive-hold' for up to 2 years with documented justification — this is an exception and will be tracked in a legal-hold register.

Action for Jasmine: finalize the one-page retention schedule and I'll prepare DPA addendum language and a DocuSign envelope for signature. Marcus — please confirm whether we need any additional operational controls for granting archive-hold (e.g., separate key custody or lockbox).

Kimberly Park
